topic: What if you could pause everyone but you?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
PAUSE EVERYONE BUT YOU?

script.text: Pause. The teacher freezes mid-word. You finish the quiz.
Pause. A fist stops an inch from your face. You stroll away.
Pause. Your best friend, frozen mid-laugh. Okay, that's creepy.
What if you could pause everyone but you?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: being isolated is linked to a twenty-nine percent higher risk of early death. That's real.
Pause enough, and you're the only one left.

science.claim: Social isolation is linked to a 29% higher risk of early death.
science.working: Pooled average across 70 studies (1980-2014), over 3.4 million participants: social isolation 29%, loneliness 26%, living alone 32% increased likelihood of mortality. An association from observational studies, so the script says 'linked to', not 'causes'.
science.source: Holt-Lunstad, Smith, Baker, Harris & Stephenson (2015), Loneliness and Social Isolation as Risk Factors for Mortality: A Meta-Analytic Review, Perspectives on Psychological Science

shots.note: Pip at his desk, palm up; the teacher at the board mid-word; the world is about to stop
the teacher frozen mid-word, chalk raised, chalk dust hanging in the air; Pip's dark shoulder soft in front
the quiz fills itself in under a fast pencil; A+ lands
a man in a suit lunges at Pip on the landing, fist out; the world stops
a huge frozen fist an inch from Pip's face; he looks at it, then smirks
Pip strolls away down the stairs, hands behind his head, the suit frozen mid-lunge
Mo at the island, head thrown back mid-laugh, frozen; Pip beside him
Pip waves a hand in front of Mo's open eyes; he doesn't blink; a frozen tear hangs in the air
Pip, uneasy; Mo soft behind him, still, staring through him
the premise over the city at dusk; Pip alone on the roof
Pip turns his head: nothing moves, no one is there
a crowd of person icons fades to grey until one orange figure is left alone
RISK OF EARLY DEATH +29% counting up; 70 STUDIES, 3.4 MILLION PEOPLE
Pip, worried; the light starts to turn red
the city goes dark in a sweep toward him; he is the only one left
